features.description: Pure command guidance contract. Define the typed data shape that describes a DontPanic command for an interactive agent: path, class, audience, examples, predecessor hints, and human escalation rule. This is a pure model only; it does not render help or execute commands.
features.acceptance: (1) A closed typed model exists for command guidance with fields for path, class, audience, examples, predecessor hints, and human escalation rule. (2) The command class vocabulary is closed and includes read-only inspection, lifecycle mutation, dispatch/paid work, configuration mutation, diagnostic inspection, and human handoff. (3) Model validation rejects unknown classes and malformed examples. (4) Tests cover valid construction, invalid class rejection, and serialization stability. (5) No existing command behavior changes.
steps: Define the pure command guidance model in a small module.
Keep the vocabulary closed and documented in code.
Add unit tests for validation and serialization.
Do not wire command help or JSON output in this feature.

features.description: Command inventory population. Populate the guidance model for the real top-level DontPanic command set. This is metadata only: it adds guidance entries and examples, but no help rendering, JSON command, or executable router.
features.acceptance: (1) The current top-level command vocabulary has guidance entries. (2) Each entry has a class, audience, examples, predecessor hints, and human escalation rule. (3) Entries cover the known workflow groups used by agents: inspection, lifecycle change, paid work, configuration change, diagnostics, and human handoff. (4) Unit tests prove inventory entries serialize through the F001 model and representative entries carry the expected metadata. (5) The inventory does not become an executable router; it is metadata only.
steps: Build the inventory entries from the current top-level command vocabulary.
Classify representative command groups with the F001 model.
Add unit tests for representative entries.
Keep all command execution out of the inventory module.

features.description: Machine-readable guidance surface. Add one read-only agent command that prints the command inventory as stable JSON so outer harnesses can inspect DontPanic affordances without scraping terminal help.
features.acceptance: (1) A read-only agent subcommand returns a versioned JSON envelope containing command guidance entries from F002. (2) The envelope includes source summary, command entries, and schema version. (3) The command does not invoke any guided command handler. (4) Tests assert schema stability and coverage parity with the F002 inventory. (5) The generated operating brief points agents to this JSON surface.
steps: Add the smallest read-only subcommand under the existing agent surface.
Render the F002 inventory to a stable JSON envelope.
Update the generated operating brief with a one-line pointer.
Add tests for read-only behavior and schema stability.

features.description: Root help agent entrypoint. Make the bare DontPanic help output tell interactive agents where to start, while keeping the full operating model in the generated brief.
features.acceptance: (1) Root help includes a concise 'Start here for AI agents' section. (2) The section names the generated brief and the JSON guidance surface. (3) The section tells agents to inspect recommended actions before mutation. (4) The text is produced from shared guidance constants or F002 metadata, not a separate command list. (5) Tests assert the root help text contains the entrypoint and does not duplicate the full brief.
steps: Add a short shared root-help snippet for agents.
Wire it into the root parser help.
Add tests for the root help output.
Avoid adding a long manual to the help page.

features.description: Workflow help policy snippets. Add class-specific agent guidance to the command help pages agents most often touch, using the F002 inventory so read-only, mutation, dispatch, diagnostics, and human handoff surfaces teach different safe behavior.
features.acceptance: (1) Representative help output for each command class contains class-appropriate agent guidance. (2) Dispatch/paid and lifecycle mutation help says not to auto-run unless DontPanic has surfaced an automatable action or the user explicitly approved it. (3) Read-only help says it is safe to inspect before mutation. (4) Human-handoff help points to the local decision surface when available. (5) Tests cover one representative command per class and prove snippets come from the shared inventory/helper, not ad hoc strings.
steps: Create small class-specific help snippets from the inventory.
Wire representative workflow commands through the shared snippet helper.
Add tests for representative commands by class.
Keep command behavior unchanged.

features.description: Versioned local guide artifact. Provide a loadable DontPanic operating guide for agent/harness environments that want a version-matched 'start here' document, without network access and without maintaining a second command manual.
features.acceptance: (1) A version-stamped local guide artifact exists and can be located or printed by an existing DontPanic surface. (2) The guide contains the start-here flow, role distinction, command classes, safe examples, local-decision handoff rule, and 'do not ask between features unless DontPanic requires human input' policy. (3) The guide is generated from or validated against the generated brief and command inventory. (4) Root help or the generated brief points to the guide locator. (5) Tests prove guide existence, required policy text, and command-inventory parity.
steps: Choose a package path and locator that fit existing DontPanic surfaces.
Create or generate the local guide artifact.
Validate guide content against the inventory.
Add tests for required policies and parity.

features.description: Future-command guidance gate. Add regression coverage and contributor guidance so new commands or newly surfaced automatable examples cannot ship without command guidance and validation coverage.
features.acceptance: (1) A test fails when the command-validation top-level vocabulary has a command with no guidance entry. (2) A test fails when a workflow-critical help page lacks an agent guidance section. (3) Automatable examples in command guidance validate against the existing command validator. (4) A developer-facing checklist explains how to add or change an agent-facing command without drift. (5) Command-validation and representative help tests pass.
steps: Add missing-guidance regression tests.
Add representative help-section regression tests.
Validate automatable examples against command validation.
Document the new-command checklist.
